neutral_facts.correct_value: Prosecutrix consistently described the appellant as short-statured with beard; facts without stating the outcome.
neutral_facts.quote: All through, the prosecutrix described appellant as gitta (short statured) man with beard
neutral_facts.reason: Claims her description later changed, contrary to judgment; also states the acquittal, revealing the outcome.

offence_severity.correct_value: Trial court sentenced the four convicts under s.376(2)(g) to ten years R.I. and fine of Rs. 2000
offence_severity.quote: The said four accused were awarded a sentence of ten years R.I. and a fine of Rs. 2000/-
offence_severity.reason: Ten years R.I. is stated, but 'minimum/maximum' framing is not in the judgment; it is the trial sentence.

attempt_completion.reason: Prosecution alleges completed rape and abduction; judgment treats offence as committed.

physical_harm.reason: Judgment notes minimal private-part injuries, no significant other injuries, and a cheek bite.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Eight accused were charged; six convicted under s.366 only in High Court, two (incl. appellant) under s.366 and s.376(2)(g)
number_of_offences.quote: eight accused were charged and prosecuted for commission of alleged offences under Section 366 and 376 (2) (g)
number_of_offences.reason: Counts accused as 'offences'; the judgment speaks of eight accused charged, not eight offences.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial or property loss is discussed in the judgment.

premeditation_planning.reason: No premeditation or planning is stated in the judgment.

motive.reason: No motive is identified in the judgment.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court found the prosecutrix's solitary evidence unreliable and not of sterling quality.

witness_credibility.reason: Court found prosecutrix not credible due to contradictions and failure to identify the kothi.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: She escaped, narrated the incident to her mother and sister, and went to the police to lodge an FIR.
post_offence_conduct.quote: As soon as she got an opportunity, she escaped from the said house and boarded the bus
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment describes her escape, narration to family, and FIR lodging, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for appellant and respondent match the judgment's listing.

investigation_status.reason: Spot maps, semen analysis, and non-examination of witnesses are all noted as investigation lacunae.

procedural_irregularity.reason: Listed irregularities (spot maps, identification parade, semen, witnesses, statements) are all in the judgment.

appeal_history.correct_value: Trial court convicted all eight under s.366 and four (KKM, V, KT, K) under s.376(2)(g)
appeal_history.quote: found present Appellant (accused) Krishan Kumar Malik, Vijay Dua, Krishan Takkar and Krishan @ Kaka, guilty for commission of offences under Section 376 (2) (g)
appeal_history.reason: Trial court convicted four, not six, under s.376(2)(g).

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Prosecution alleged abduction and gang-rape by eight accused; counsel relied on s.53A CrPC and DNA-test requirement.
prosecution_argument.quote: brought to our notice by learned counsel for the Respondent-State
prosecution_argument.reason: Abduction/rape case is correct, but claim that FIR and statements sufficed is not in the judgment.

defence_argument.correct_value: Defence counsel stated, after verification from the appellant's wife, that he is 5'6" tall; other points were the court's own findings.
defence_argument.quote: a statement before the Bench has been made by learned counsel for Appellant, after verification from the Appellant's wife, that he is 5' 6" tall
defence_argument.reason: Height contention is supported, but the broader defence argument, including DNA and spot maps, is not recorded as counsel's submission.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Solitary prosecutrix evidence must inspire confidence; corroboration and investigative lacunae were applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Section 6 Indian Evidence Act, 1872; Section 53A CrPC, 1973; Taylor's Principles and Practice of Medical Jurisprudence (2nd Edn., 1965); Black's Law Dictionary
precedent_relied_upon.quote: KRISHAN KUMAR MALIK v. STATE OF HARYANA
precedent_relied_upon.reason: The case itself is listed as precedent; it is the judgment under review, not an authority relied on.

sentencing_rationale.reason: No sentencing rationale applies; appellant was acquitted.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Court used the handicap and investigative lapses to doubt the prosecution, not as sentencing mitigation.
